title: Vector sanity gates and config-triggered regression probes
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Model or serving configuration changes (quantization profile, batching, kernel selection, model variant mapping) have caused subtle degradation in reranker/embedding outcomes in past rollouts. We need an automated, config-triggered evaluation and gating system that runs fast offline probes and drift checks before allowing rollouts to proceed. Goal: catch >3% absolute recall/precision regressions on critical query sets, and detect distribution drift that correlates with degraded user-visible metrics.

Scope: offline evaluation jobs that run when: 1) model version changes, 2) quantization/precision profile changes, 3) routing/policy changes that remap requests to different model variants, 4) major runtime kernel or batch-size default updates. The job should run a mix of lightweight production-sampled probes + synthetic perturbations.

Metrics to compute (per-route and global): recall@k (k=1,3,5), precision@k, MRR, nearest-neighbor-overlap (NNO) between baseline and candidate, cosine-similarity distribution KS statistic, centroid shift for key segments, and a small set of targeted binary correctness checks from golden Q/A pairs. Each metric must be computed overall and grouped by customer cohort and by sequence-length bucket.

Drift checks: run KS-test on similarity distributions; thresholded NNO drop (e.g., NNO@50 drop > 6%); centroid shift normalized by baseline variance; alarm on multi-metric degradation patterns rather than a single noisy signal.

Automation: config change triggers job in eval-service. Job produces a result bundle with metrics, statistical significance (bootstrap CI), and a compact human-readable summary. If any gating rule is violated (config-level threshold AND customer-impact rule), the change is marked as failed and a rollback / block on rollout is applied. If metrics are borderline, create a canary rollout recommendation instead of full block.

Integration points: Console dashboards (per-route quality panel), rollout service (can block rollouts), CI (PR checks for model/quant changes), Slack alerts and PagerDuty for high-impact failures, telemetry tags emitted from runtime (model_version, quant_profile, kernel_tag, batch_hint, route_id). Stored results go to eval-results-store (timeseries + JSON blob) and to metrics pipeline for historical trend analysis.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Define probe sets: production-sampled "lite" probes (2k queries), golden canonical queries (500), and synthetic perturbations (paraphrase/noise/locale).
2) Extend eval-service to accept "config-change" trigger and to annotate runs with provenance metadata.
3) Implement NNO and KS tests in eval library; expose bootstrap CI and effect-size.
4) Add gating rules config with default thresholds and per-customer overrides.
5) Wire results to Console and rollout service.
6) Create an incident/playbook for triaging failed gates (who to ping, quick rollback steps, when to proceed with manual approval).

Trade-offs/Notes:
- Lightweight probes must complete within ~15 minutes to avoid slowing deployments; heavier full-suite runs can be asynchronous and only used for scheduled audits.
- Thresholds should be conservative to avoid false positives; we accept occasional manual approvals early on.
- Per-customer baselines reduce noise but require storing historical embeddings/keys and privacy considerations.

Success criteria: automated blocking of at least one simulated regression in canary tests during rollout dry-run, visible dashboards with per-route baselines, and reduced undetected production regressions in next quarter.
acceptance_criteria: Eval-service runs triggered automatically on model/config change and returns a result bundle
Computed metrics include recall@1/3/5, precision@1/3/5, MRR, NNO@50, cosine KS-stat, centroid shift with bootstrap CI
Gating rules can be configured per-project and enforce block/canary/allow decisions
Console shows a per-route quality panel and links to the last eval bundle for each rollout
Rollout service reads gate decision and prevents full rollout when a gate is failed
Slack alert + regression artifact (PR/rollout ID + top failing queries) produced for any failed high-impact gate
Documentation: playbook for triage + runbook for manual override published in Confluence
